title: Add six records-history record types with validation to athena-data
summary: Narrowed job 1 of records-history (§10, D111) to the schema only: add landing-intent, landing, intervention, checkpoint, legacy-exempt and import-manifest record types to athena-data, with validation, round-trip and rejection tests, doc comments citing the design, and a CHANGELOG entry. The writer and host-rules check are excluded. Audience: the maintainer and the verifier running cargo test.

defaults_applied.how: Round-trip and rejection tests; cargo test and clippy pass.
Schema only, per the user's narrowing.
Criteria run tests that exercise round-trip and rejection.
Doc comments cite the design for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Existing records.rs conventions (serde deny_unknown_fields, schema tag, pretty JSON) are followed; new types may live in records.rs or a new module.
The new 'intervention' record is distinct from the existing InterventionCategory enum; naming must avoid clashing with it.
The writer and host-rules check are later jobs and out of scope per the user's reply.
No new crate dependency is needed; if one is added it is justified under buy-first.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test -p athena-data: each of the six new record types (landing-intent, landing, intervention, checkpoint, legacy-exempt, import-manifest) serializes to JSON with a schema tag and deserializes back to an equal value.

Run cargo test -p athena-data: validation rejects malformed examples for the new types: an empty required field, an unknown field, a malformed sha (not 40 lowercase hex), and a wrong schema tag. Valid examples pass.
Run cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets and cargo fmt --check: all pass. Existing records and history-check tests are unchanged and still pass.

Public new items carry doc comments citing docs/design/records-history.md (§5.3, §4 or §8 as relevant) and D111. Fields follow the design: landing-intent has PR number, head sha, head tree sha, expected base, job ids; landing has PR number, head sha, host commit, merge method, ordered commits (sha, tree) with job and verification, and the intent it fulfills; intervention has declarer, reason and commit sha; import-manifest has C0 and per-path blob id and SHA-256; legacy-exempt has entries with sha and reason.
No writer, no host-rules check, and no git-branch code is added. No code in athena-core, athena-cli or athena-gate uses the new types. records/ on main and the history check have no diff.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry naming the six new record types in athena-data.

out_of_scope: The compare-and-swap writer and bounded retry for athena/records
Any change to records/ on main or the history check
Wiring the types into athena-core, athena-cli or athena-gate
